newsitem.title: USA: NRG in pact with Millennium Petrochemicals.
newsitem.headline: NRG in pact with Millennium Petrochemicals.

text.p: NRG Energy Inc said Friday it signed an agreement with Millennium Petrochemicals Inc to build and operate a 117 MW, inside-the-fence gas cogeneration plant at its Morris, Ill. industrial facility.
The cogeneration plant, fueled with natural gas and some process methane gas, will supply the industrial facility's steam and electrical needs. NRG will market the excess capacity and energy.
Construction is expected to begin in October of 1997 and commercial operation is targeted for year-end 1998.

"The project will enhance Millennium Petrochemicals' competitiveness by providing a long-term, reliable source of low-cost electric power and steam to our facility," Ralph Wolter, engineering manager for Millennium said.

"The Millennium project is consistent with our strategy to construct and operate state-of-the-art facilities for targeted industries, such as the chemical industry, that will provide electricity, process steam and services at extremely competitive rates," said Craig Mataczynski, NRG vice president U.S. Business Development.
Millennium Petrochemicals, a subsidiary of Millennium Chemicals Inc, is the largest domestic producer of polyethylene and a major supplier of performance polymers and select chemicals.

NRG, a subsidiary of Northern States Power Co, is a large independent power producer with participation in over 7,000 MW of projects in the United States, Europe, Latin America, Australia and the Pacific Rim.
